chapter: Arranging career and the JPJ Quartet
title: Bands and singers Budd has arranged for
summary: At Hinton's request Budd lists the leaders he has written for, from Hines to Ivory Joe Hunter's 'I Almost Lost My Mind'.

bands.name: Ina Ray Hutton and Her Orchestra

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Budd, that was beautiful. I'd just like to stop right now. There's a couple of things I wanted to ask you. First, I'm going to get to you. There's a couple of stories you promised have to tell me about Earl Hines that were really funny.
So we'll digress back to that later.

But this has been so interesting in talking to you about all of these different organizations and bands and people that you've been involved with, I wanted just for right now for the sake of the record give the names of -- in your whole career some of these great bands that you've written for so everybody will know. Because this is -- I don't think this has ever been told before, all of the things that you
-- all the people that you've written and contributed your great talents to. So just start naming them off. You started and with and Gus Arnheim -- your mother was a maid in this place --
So just bring it on down from there.

Well, I wrote for Gus Arnner and and I wrote for him (inaudible). I wrote for Earl Hines; I wrote for Jerry Jerome as I told you as staff arranger for NBC. I wrote for Billy Eckstein, Sarah Vaughn, and I wrote for Teddy Wilson when he was at CBS with his program. And I wrote for Fletcher Henderson, I wrote for Dizzy Gillespie, I wrote for Woody Herman, I wrote for Gene Krupa, I wrote for Auld George Yorks, I wrote for Ina Rae Hutton, I wrote for Boyd Rabin, and I wrote for Jimmy Noon.

Clarinet player. Wrote for Louis Armstrong, wrote for George E. Lee, John Kirby, I wrote -- used to write a lot of arrangements for RCA Victor. They would call me in to do different things, even with springs. That's way back. I wrote for Decca Records, I wrote -- I was musical director for Atlantic Records, I wrote for MGM Records when Ivory Joe Hunter was singing for them and we did this tune "I Almost Lost My Mind."
This is what made this guy Pat Boone so great. He stole the exact same arrangement that I had written for Ivory Joe Hunter.
